observations: The woman quietly lifts/holds the supported record sleeves, lowers them into the open box, and settles her hands on the exposed aligned top edges. This is an actual completed placement, followed by a restrained pause; it is not a full clear withdrawal of both hands.

Every native keeper hand/record contact frame was inspected. Both hands remain connected through the wrists and retain plausible edge support; the sleeve bottoms disappear progressively behind the box front as expected. No autonomous record travel, box penetration, extra limb, abrupt grip teleport or unsupported stack jump was observed.

Her downcast, depleted face and economical movements remain consistent. The man watches with a tense, concerned posture; no abrupt hostile lunge, grabbing, recovery smile or cheerful performance was observed.

Late stillness is a natural resting action with small image/body changes, not inserted identical-frame repetition. Box/table/room geometry and character clothing remain coherent throughout the keeper at the reviewed scale.
limitations: This shot communicates quiet withdrawn ordering in the surrounding story; tidying alone does not diagnose suicidal intent. Fear and recognition remain contextual and need the planned subsequent shots.
The final approximately three seconds are deliberately restrained. The scene should not be described as rapid continuous new action or as a hand-release demonstration.
No final join, complete-film emotional pacing, exact lyric articulation or subjective listening acceptance is granted by this source gate.

observations: All five distinct band members remain present and spatially stable. The singer keeps the microphone supported near his mouth, changes head/torso posture, then raises and rotates his free left hand into an open-palm chest-level gesture.

The drummer performs repeated alternating lift/lower strokes with two supported sticks. The guitarist makes multiple small pick/strum wrist cycles and maintains fretting contact; the bassist makes small plucking/fretting changes. The keyboardist has restrained finger/hand changes compatible with ensemble chord playing. This is visible ensemble action rather than a static pose moved only by a camera transform.

Native consecutive contact crops show connected wrists/forearms, supported instrument bodies/straps and plausible playing surfaces. No gross body morph, floating instrument, extra arm, disappearing player or hand passing through an instrument was observed in the keeper.

Singer hand linework briefly softens during its turning/lifting movement around raw frames 80–94. The hand and sleeve remain connected on a smooth spatial trajectory and settle into a readable open palm; this is nonblocking fine motion softness at this 896-pixel-wide ensemble scale.
Drum hardware, keys stand, guitar/bass straps and stage positions stay coherent. Small cymbal/head/garment movement reads as performance rather than autonomous prop displacement.
limitations: Wide-shot finger and facial detail is small and sometimes soft. This gate establishes coherent user-visible action at the delivered source scale, not perfect individual digit/string/key reconstruction.
The guitar, bass and keyboard motion is restrained and includes ordinary held poses/short pauses. The wide shot is appropriate as an ensemble insert, not proof of a virtuoso close-up performance.
Exact played notes, beat-by-beat drum impacts, chord fingering, lyric phoneme sync and subjective human hearing were not established. No claim of perfect music synchronization is made.
Full-film sequencing, neighboring shot joins and further generation batches remain independently reviewable.
